free_tier.stated: 5 GB maximum per uploaded file (Generic). No per-project or per-namespace package storage cap is documented; the package registry is explicitly excluded from the 10 GiB project storage limit.

retention.stated: Artifacts expire in 30 days, packages do not.

egress.terms: Free and Cloudflare-fronted. GitLab.com is behind Cloudflare and blobs are served from Google Cloud Storage / the GitLab CDN (cdn.registry.gitlab-static.net). No egress billing for public projects.

tooling: GitLab REST API v4 (`PUT /projects/:id/packages/generic/:package_name/:version/:file_name`, `GET .../package_files/:id/download`), glab CLI, python-gitlab (has generic package support, merged), goreleaser pushes generic packages natively (PR #2745 merged). Works with plain curl — no special client needed.
chaining: Unlimited projects per namespace (no project-count cap is documented on GitLab.com; the only new limits are 3 top-level *groups* for accounts created after 2026-01-27, and the personal namespace does not count). Each project is its own unbounded package bucket at 5 GB/file. N projects x unlimited package versions x 5 GB. Multiply again by additional free namespaces (3 groups + personal) and by unlimited free accounts.
limits_note: 5 GB per file (Generic / Maven / npm / NuGet / PyPI / Conan); 10 GB for ML models (upload capped at 5 GB); 1 GB for Terraform state; Helm only 5 MB. Anonymous read of public project packages; writes need a token. Repository/LFS Git push limited to 5 GiB per request, irrelevant to packages.

reliability_note: Snippets, packages and job artifacts count toward *namespace* storage as a display/billing figure but are not enforced as a cap — enforcement is per-project on repo+LFS only. GitLab could start enforcing namespace storage at any time; it has never done so for packages. Artifacts expire in 30 days, packages do not.
